la:noun:pactio.gloss: The act of agreeing or covenanting; an agreement, covenant, contract, bargain, pact, treaty, truce.
senses: The act of agreeing or covenanting; an agreement, covenant, contract, bargain, pact, treaty, truce.
la:noun:pactio.html:
pactĭo, ōnis, f.
paciscor
.
In gen., an agreeing, covenanting; an agreement, covenant, contract, bargain, pact (syn. pactum): est autem pactio duorum plurinmve in idem placitum et consensum,: in pactionibus faciendis legem spectare,: pactionem facere de aliquā re,, and 14, 40: nefarias cum multis pactiones conflare,: pactionem cum aliquo facere, ut, etc.,: condiciones pactionesque bellicas perturbare perjurio,; : arma per pactionem tradere,: summā fide in pactione manere,: talibus pactionibus pacem facere,conditions,: interpositā pactione,; : pactionem de republicā facere,: collegam suum Antonium pactione provinciae perpulerat, ne, etc.,by making over to him his province according to agreement,: pactionem nuptialem facere,: praemiorum,a promise,.—
In partic.
An agreement, compact, between the farmers general and the inhabitants of a province: pactiones cum aliquo conficere,; .—
A corrupt bargaining, an underhand agreement or compact: nonnullos pactionis suspicionem non vitasse,: Aulum spe pactionis perpulit, uti, etc.,; cf. .—
A truce: aut pax aut pactio,.—
Pactio verborum, a form of words: ex pactione verborum, quibus jusjurandum comprehenditur,on account of the form of oath,; cf.: deos cum pactionibus adorare et formulis,—
A marriage-contract: hic eam rem volt, scio, mecum adire ad pactionem (= mecum pacisci),.

la:verb:paco#2.html:
pāco, ăvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
pax
,
to bring into a state of peace and quietness, to make peaceful, to quiet, pacify, subdue, soothe (class.; cf.: pacifico, placo).
Lit.: pacare Amanum,: omnem Galliam,: qui nuper pacati erant,: civitates,: Hispanias,: bimarem Isthmon,: regiones,: Asiam,: Erymanthi nemora,: MARE A PRAEDONIBVS, Monum. Ancyr. fin. ap. Grut. 233; .—
Transf., of things as objects: incultae pacantur vomere silvae,are subdued, tilled,: et pacare metu silvas,: saltus remotos pacabat cornu,: incertos animi aestus,to quiet,; cf. feras,to tame,: dolorem,.—Hence, pācā-tus, a, um, P. a., pacified, quieted, peaceful, quiet, calm, tranquil, undisturbed (opp. hostilis; class.).
Lit.: pacatae tranquillaeque civitates,: in provinciā pacatissimā,: pacatissima et quietissima pars,: nec hospitale quicquam pacatumve,: pacato agmine transire,: pacati status aëris,: pacata posse omnia mente tueri,: mare,: vultus,: pacatus mitisque adsis,: coloni,.—As subst.: pācātum, i, n., a friendly country: vagi milites in pacato,: ex pacatis praedas agere,i. e. from countries at peace with Rome,: qui medius inter pacata et hostilia fuit, Danubius et Rhenus,.—
Trop.: oratio pacatior,: cujus ne pacatam quidem nequitiam quisquam ferre posset,.—And in the neutr. as subst.: nec diu in pacato mansit gens,on friendly terms,.—Hence, adv.: pācātē, peaceably, quietly (post-Aug.).—Comp.: pacatius ad reliqua secessimus,; .—Sup.: pacatissime et commodissime,.

la:verb:pacifico.gloss: to make, negotiate or arrange peace
senses: to make, negotiate or arrange peace
la:verb:pacifico.html:
pācĭfĭco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a. (ante- and post-class.; also, pācĭfĭcor, ātus,
v. dep.;v.in the foll., and cf. P.) [paxfacio], to make or conclude a peace (not in Cic. or Cæs.).
Lit.: quo Metellus initio, Jugurthā pacificante, praesidium imposuerat,at the beginning of Jugurtha's negotiations for peace,: legati pacificatum venerunt,; cf. ; .—
As a deponent: pacificari cum altero statuit,: pacificatus cum Carthaginiensibus,: set satine tecum pacificatus sum, Antipho? have I quite made my peace with you? i. e. are you entirely reconciled? .—
Transf., in gen., to pacify, appease (poet.): caelestes pacificasset,: divos,: mentem suam,to soothe, quiet,: aures Pieriis modis,, praef. 20.

la:verb:paciscor.gloss: to make a bargain, contract or agreement with
senses: to make a bargain, contract or agreement with
la:verb:paciscor.html:
păciscor, pactus, 3,
v. dep. n. and a. (act. collat. form, v.supra) [1. paco], to make a bargain, contract, or agreement with any one; to covenant, agree, stipulate, bargain, contract respecting any thing (cf.: transigo, stipulor, pango).
Lit.
In gen.
Neutr.: pacisci cum illo paululā pecuniā potes,; ; : paciscitur magnā mercede cum Celtiberorum principibus, ut, etc.,; cf.: pacti sunt inter se, ut die statutā,; ; ; cf. esp. : votis pacisci, Ne Cypriae Tyriaeque merces Addant avaro divitias mari (= votis transigere cum dis),: de mercedibus,.—
Act.: quae pacisci modo scis, set quod pacta's, non scis solvere,: argentum, arg. 1, 9: quam (provinciam) sibi pactus erat,: rem,: pecuniam cum aliquo, Auct. B. Alex. 55: omnibus proscriptis, reditum salutemque pactus est,: ab aliquo vitam,; so, pactus in singulos (homines) minas decem a tyranno,: cum Xerxe nuptias filiae,.—With object-clause: Leucippo fieri pactus uterque gener,: dimitti (eum) pactus, si, etc.,.—In part. fut. pass.: ut firma fierent paciscenda,.—
In partic., of a marriage-contract, to betroth a woman (syn.: despondeo, spondeo): ex quā pactus esset vir domo, in matrimonium duceret,: Etutam pacto fratri eum invidisse,.—
Trop., to barter, hazard, stake (poet.): vitam pro laude,: letum pro laude,: aevum pro luce,.

la:other:Pacuvius.html:
Pācŭvĭus (Pācŭus), i, m.,
the name of a Roman gens. So esp. Pacuvius, a celebrated Roman poet, a native of Brundisium, nephew of Ennius, and contemporary of P. Scipio Africanus, ; ; ; ; ; . He is also said to have distinguished himself as a painter, .—Sync. form: Pacui discipulus dicor, porro is fuit Enni, Enniu' musarum, Varr. ap. ; Jan.—Hence,
Pā-cŭvĭānus, a, um, adj., Pacuvian: physicus,: testudo,described by Pacuvius,: ex quibus est Pacuvianum illud: nam si qui, etc.,that Pacuvian verse,.
